build: Decibel and Eagle Soft Incorporated side A, Eagle Soft Incorporated side B

extra: D4 module matched to the private disk directory and captured in VICE

comments.text: Relocated entry word $2E68 followed by body length $062A for D4.
Test the argument in A. A negative value releases the two display items, zero prepares the cockpit, and a positive value enters the gauge update dispatch.
Release the private disk resources with first ID byte ASCII 4 and second ID bytes $28 and $29.
Resolve resource IDs 4/$28 and 4/$29, skip their six-byte headers, and store their data bases at $33D0 and $33D2 before setting up the instrument state.
For A equal to 1, compare $42 with its copy at $33CA and run the instrument update only if they differ.
Immediate subtrahend patched at $2F67 from the scaled engine speed plus $42. The difference, adjusted by $4C when subtraction borrows, selects the tachometer angle.
Compare speed $41 with its cached value, then scale it through $31F7, install the speed-specific tables and call the common needle renderer.
Immediate subtrahend patched at $2FB9 from the scaled road speed. The subtraction and borrow adjustment select the speedometer angle. The path also sets $1F61 to $83.

Use $0E to select the gauge's picture source. Classify the input against $2D, $5A and $87, update the gauge sprite coordinates, and compute its line endpoint from the selected horizontal and vertical lookups.
For quadrants 1 and 2, subtract the indexed horizontal table value from the maximum sprite column in $10.
Low operand for the reflected horizontal lookup. Both gauge paths patch it from the descriptor at $3223.
High operand for the horizontal subtraction. The other path at $3040 loads the same table value directly.
Low operand for the unreflected horizontal lookup at $3040.
High operand for the unreflected horizontal lookup. The resulting column goes to $1E before the routine chooses the vertical path.
For quadrants 0 and 1, subtract the indexed vertical table value from the maximum sprite row in $11.
Low operand for the reflected vertical lookup. It is patched from the descriptor at $3226.
High operand for the vertical subtraction. Quadrants 2 and 3 load the row directly at $3056.
Low operand for the unreflected vertical lookup at $3056.
High operand for the unreflected vertical lookup. The selected row follows into $1F.
Compare the endpoint pair against the saved coordinates for this gauge and return if unchanged. Otherwise clear its 64-byte sprite buffer before preparing the line.
Take absolute coordinate differences and retain their signs in $29 and $2B. Choose the larger difference as the main step and calculate the other step as a fixed-point ratio through $3199.
Draw at the current coordinates and, within the horizontal bound, at the next pixel. Update the fixed-point coordinates in the direction of the endpoint until the main coordinate matches.
Resolve the pixel's sprite byte from the row stride table at $3399 and X-byte table at $3369. Mask the picture source byte with $3381 and OR the result into the sprite.
Indexed absolute read from the cockpit artwork used as a pixel mask. Gauge selection patches its two address bytes at $2FD7 and $2FDD.
Low byte of the artwork base after the six-byte resource header is skipped.
High byte of the source artwork pointer. The following instructions select the source pixel bit, OR it into the destination sprite byte and restore the shared pointer low byte.
Align the denominator by shifting, subtract it from the numerator when possible, and roll each resulting quotient bit into $2D and $2E. Return the fixed-point step in A and X.
Patch the two immediate arguments to the driving-engine call at $0200. Preserve $12, $13, $16 and $17 across the call, then return its result.
Immediate A argument to the scaling call at $320D. The wrapper copies the original A here before saving its zero-page temporaries.
Immediate X argument for the driving-engine scaling call. The wrapper restores four zero-page values after the call and temporarily saves the result in the return operand.
Immediate return value patched at $3210 with the result from $0200 before the saved zero-page values are restored.
Tagged little-endian addresses for the gauge setup. The code uses the operands as data, including $3223 and $3226 for endpoint table pointers.
Low address byte of the horizontal endpoint table, copied into both horizontal load operands.
High address byte of the horizontal endpoint table followed by the tag for the next address record.
Low address byte of the vertical endpoint table, copied into both vertical load operands.
High address byte of the vertical endpoint table followed by the tag for the driving setup pointer.
Low address byte of the driving setup descriptors at $322B. Cockpit initialization returns it in X.
High byte of the descriptor list address returned in Y from the cockpit setup routine.

Three-byte records used by the driving setup at $7307. The operand words give the gear ratio, acceleration curve, steering-wheel offsets, gear-lever coordinates and alternate shift map. The following immediate operands set the steering-wheel centre.
Indexed by half the steering magnitude. The engine subtracts the entry from $6E and adds the cockpit vertical offset before updating the sprite Y coordinate.
Horizontal offset magnitude indexed by half the steering magnitude. The engine applies the steering sign and adds the cockpit horizontal centre before updating the sprite X coordinate.
Horizontal sprite coordinates indexed by quadrant and gauge at $3003.
Vertical sprite coordinates written by $300C. The table index includes four entries per gauge.
Horizontal pivot coordinate for the selected quadrant, copied to $1C.
Vertical pivot coordinate used as the line origin in $1D.
Per-quadrant adjustment added by the sprite pixel routine when it selects a source row.
Ninety endpoint rows in the 21-pixel sprite. The loads patched at $3051 and $3057 use this table. Quadrants 0 and 1 subtract the selected row from 20.
Ninety endpoint columns in the 24-pixel sprite. The loads patched at $303B and $3041 use this table. Quadrants 1 and 2 subtract the selected column from 23.
Twenty-four horizontal pixel indices mapped to the three sprite byte columns in groups of eight.
The eight single-bit masks repeated for each of three sprite byte columns.
Row offset multiplied by three. The plotter uses this to find the destination byte of the 24-pixel-wide sprite row.
Row offset multiplied by six. The plotter combines this with the selected column and source offset to read the picture mask.
Two low bytes locating the needle sprite buffers in RAM.
High bytes paired with $33C5 to locate each 64-byte sprite allocation.
Saved index after the quadrant-specific adjustment at $302C.
Input cache used by the A-equals-one update path at $2F23.
Speed last processed by the handler at $2F78.
Horizontal endpoint cache indexed by gauge, initialized by $2EB1 and compared by $305F.
Second gauge horizontal endpoint cache. Gauge initialization sets it to $FF to force a first redraw.
Vertical endpoint cache selected by the same gauge index.
Two little-endian picture addresses, populated by skipping the six-byte resource headers during initialization.
High address byte of the tachometer artwork source. Setup carries into it when skipping the six-byte header.
Low address byte of the speedometer artwork source. The common plotter selects it for the second gauge.
High address byte of the speedometer artwork source. The selection routine copies it to the indexed load at $3189.
Extra offset into the picture source chosen using the gauge quadrant.
Fifteen authored sprite bytes copied to $E440 after the 64-byte allocation is cleared.
Gear-lever sprite X targets indexed by the selected gear. The first value also seeds the idle target at $1F5C.
Gear-lever sprite Y targets indexed by the selected gear. The first value supplies the intermediate row used while the X coordinate is changing.
Eight directions per current gear for alternate shifting. The engine forms eight times the gear plus direction minus one and stores the selected result to $45.
Fixed-point scaling factors indexed by gear at $9802. The engine uses the ratio and road speed to calculate engine speed.

Cockpit module tail beginning with acceleration values indexed by engine speed. The driving engine scales the selected value by gear, subtracts the speed-dependent term, and adds the resulting nonnegative amount to the road-speed accumulator.
